entities.name: Abu al-Salim al-Marini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ibrahim ibn Ali Abu Salim, known as Abu al-Salim al-Marini, was a Marinid ruler who reigned from 1359 to 1361 during the height of the Medieval era. Born in Fez, a crucial center of Islamic learning and governance in North Africa, Abu al-Salim came to power in 1359 following the reign of Abu Bakr ibn Faris, representing the complex dynamics of dynastic succession that characterized Marinid rule.

During his relatively brief tenure as sovereign, Abu al-Salim demonstrated a commitment to administrative integration by appointing the renowned scholar Abd ibn Khaldun to the prestigious position of mazalim, a role overseeing justice and grievances within the realm. This decision underscored the interplay between political authority and intellectual authority that defined Medieval governance, particularly in the Islamic world where religious and administrative functions were deeply intertwined.

However, Abu al-Salim's rule faced significant challenges from both civilian and military factions within the Marinid state. By 1361, after a period of internal turbulence and political instability during the autumn months, he was forced to relinquish power. He was succeeded by Tashfin ibn Ali, marking another transition in the succession of Marinid monarchs. Abu al-Salim's reign, though short-lived, contributed to the broader patterns of Marinid dynastic governance and left an imprint on the political structures that would influence the region for generations to come.
